comparison.title: Why this beats
comparison.description: Most translator apps ignore tones and drop your history the moment you close them. Here's what's different.

rows.title: How you start
rows.us: Speak in English or Chinese and get a translation right away.
rows.them: Type your sentence out first, character by character.

rows.them: Text-only results, so tones are left to guesswork.

rows.them: Each translation vanishes once you close the app.

rows.title: Both directions

faq.heading: Frequently asked
faq.sub: Common questions about translating between English and Chinese.

items.q: Does it show real Chinese characters, not pinyin?
items.a: Yes, translations appear in proper Chinese characters, matched to the meaning of your sentence.

items.q: Can it translate spoken Chinese into English?
items.a: Yes — speak Chinese into the mic and get an English translation as text, with audio playback available.

items.q: How do I know I'm getting the tones right?
items.a: Tap the speaker icon on any Chinese translation to hear it read aloud, so you can hear the correct tones instead of guessing.
Yes. The service is free for everyone — no subscription and no quota. Sign in with email, Google or Apple only if you want your history attached to an account instead of this browser.

items.q: Do I need a Chinese keyboard or input method?
items.a: No, the app displays Chinese characters automatically — you don't need to type them yourself.

items.q: Can I keep a running conversation instead of separate lookups?
items.a: Yes, each language pair keeps its own history, so a conversation stays together instead of scattering across separate translations.

finalCta.heading: Start your English to Chinese
finalCta.sub: Speak or type, read or hear it in Chinese — free to try, no sign-up.
